note: Adjudicated accidental and house-orthography variants. The witnesses agree on the substantive text. Proper body and separately expanded RG115a conclusion have distinct source scopes; expansion accents and punctuation are house realization.

adjudicated.ruling: The j-form against this edition's i-form, by the house rule in ORTHOGRAPHY.md. This edition prints i because the books it edits do: the approved 1962 Benziger printing sets Iesu, Ioánnem, iube and maiestátis throughout, and so does the Ordo Missae of Pallottinum, Poznań 1963, which is the book a Polish reader is most likely to hold. The mid-century hand missals print j; neither spelling is a different word, and the apparatus records theirs.

The separately expanded RG115a conclusion uses the selected house spelling, punctuation and capitalization, not a literal complete conclusion on the proper page. The pinned digital accidental remains recorded exactly.
